QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_37

question.text: Under the workbook's guidance on deadweight, what is the CORRECT principle the SIA should apply when assessing a programme's net additional impact?

answer.text: Use dead weights to subtract what would have happened anyway, so the report avoids overclaiming and presents net additional impact
Report only the gross programme output without any adjustment
Ignore counterfactual conditions because they cannot be measured
Apply a fixed deduction percentage regardless of context

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports the use of dead weights to estimate what would have happened anyway and to avoid overclaiming. Subtracting deadweight from the gross outcome gives the net additional impact that can be attributed to the programme. The Trap: Reporting gross output ignores deadweight. Ignoring counterfactuals contradicts the workbook guidance. A fixed deduction without context lacks evidence-based justification. Note: Disclose the deadweight assumptions and basis (such as comparator data or published rates) so users can evaluate the net impact calculation.
